rituals.vibeLine: Your brain picked the one explanation starring you. Shocking.
rituals.hook: One slow reply, five possible universes.
rituals.predict: Guess how many non-personal explanations you can produce before your brain returns to “they’re upset with me.”
rituals.play: Spin through five reasons for the delay: busy, driving, asleep, forgot, battery, family, work, unsure what to say, anything plausible. Only one slot may be about you.
rituals.catch: Notice how much certainty the personal explanation loses once alternatives occupy the wheel.
rituals.reveal: A delayed reply contains very little information about motive.
rituals.mindBend: A slow reply is a lousy relationship detective.

rituals.name: SAME TEXT, THREE VOICES
rituals.title: SAME TEXT, THREE VOICES
rituals.targetPattern: Assigning emotional tone to text
rituals.target_pattern: Assigning emotional tone to text
rituals.precise_subpattern: Assigning emotional tone to text
rituals.vibeLine: Your brain hired a voice actor without checking with the sender.
rituals.hook: Text messages arrive without vocal cords.
rituals.predict: Guess which reading changes your reaction most: warm, bored, irritated.
rituals.play: Take the exact message and read it three times in your head: warm voice, distracted voice, annoyed voice. Change no words.
rituals.catch: Notice how much meaning moves when only the imagined voice changes.
rituals.reveal: Text carries words; tone is partly reconstructed by the reader.
rituals.mindBend: Your brain can hear a tone that was never actually sent.
rituals.ritualCard:
Text messages arrive without vocal cords.
Take the exact message and read it three times in your head: warm voice, distracted voice, annoyed voice. Change no words.
Guess which reading changes your reaction most: warm, bored, irritated.
Notice how much meaning moves when only the imagined voice changes. Text carries words; tone is partly reconstructed by the reader.

rituals.name: STRANGER MEMORY TEST
rituals.title: STRANGER MEMORY TEST
rituals.targetPattern: Overestimating how much others notice
rituals.target_pattern: Overestimating how much others notice
rituals.precise_subpattern: Overestimating how much others notice
rituals.vibeLine: You barely remember them. They probably are not writing your biography either.
rituals.hook: How closely are people really studying you?
rituals.predict: Guess how many details you remember about the last stranger you passed.
rituals.play: Think of the last stranger you saw. Without cheating, recall their shoes, hair, facial expression and one flaw. Count what you genuinely remember.
rituals.catch: Compare that memory with how closely you imagine strangers are tracking your details.
rituals.reveal: People are usually the centre of their own attention, just as you are of yours.
rituals.mindBend: You are highly visible to yourself. That is not the same as being highly monitored by everyone else.

rituals.vibeLine: The rejection was specific. Your brain filed for nationwide distribution.
rituals.hook: One “no” is trying to write a biography about you.
rituals.predict: Guess how many extra claims were added after the actual refusal.
rituals.play: Say the smallest factual sentence: “They said no to ___.” Then list every larger conclusion your mind attached: nobody wants me, I’m unlikeable, this always happens, I will be alone.
rituals.catch: Count how many conclusions were not literally contained in the original no.
rituals.reveal: A refusal can be painful and specific at the same time.
rituals.mindBend: “No to this” and “no to you as a human” are different sentences.

rituals.targetPattern: Overpredicting social awkwardness
rituals.target_pattern: Overpredicting social awkwardness
rituals.precise_subpattern: Overpredicting social awkwardness
rituals.vibeLine: Your dread finally had to put an actual prediction on the table.
rituals.hook: Make a tiny bet on the first ten seconds of the next interaction.
rituals.predict: Guess exactly what awkward thing will happen in the first ten seconds—not the whole encounter.
rituals.play: Before the next safe interaction, write one concrete prediction: silence, stumble, weird look, no reply. After 10 sec, check only that prediction.
rituals.catch: Compare feared movie length with the tiny piece of reality you actually tested.
rituals.reveal: Specific forecasts can be corrected; vague dread cannot.
rituals.mindBend: Anxiety loves forecasts too blurry to ever be proven wrong.

rituals.name: EMPTY CHAIR FRIEND TEST
rituals.title: EMPTY CHAIR FRIEND TEST
rituals.targetPattern: Different standards for self and others
rituals.target_pattern: Different standards for self and others
rituals.precise_subpattern: Different standards for self and others
rituals.vibeLine: Interesting how the sentence changes when somebody else has to hear it.
rituals.hook: Give your inner critic an audience it did not expect.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the exact sentence sounds fair when aimed at someone you care about.
rituals.play: Put an empty chair opposite you. Imagine a friend made the same mistake. Say your self-criticism to the chair word for word.
rituals.catch: Check if your tone, wording or certainty suddenly feels excessive.
rituals.reveal: Distance reveals standards that feel normal only when pointed inward.
rituals.mindBend: If the sentence becomes cruel when a friend is in the chair, it was already cruel when you were.

rituals.vibeLine: The essay was mostly trying to control the grade.
rituals.hook: Make the apology smaller than the anxiety around it.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the one-sentence version will feel dangerously incomplete.

rituals.name: NO-PERMISSION MICRO-CHOICE
rituals.title: NO-PERMISSION MICRO-CHOICE
rituals.targetPattern: Checking harmless choices with others
rituals.target_pattern: Checking harmless choices with others
rituals.precise_subpattern: Checking harmless choices with others
rituals.vibeLine: No poll, no group chat, somehow still a legal choice.
rituals.hook: Make one tiny decision that does not require a committee meeting.
rituals.predict: Guess how uncomfortable it will feel to choose without checking anyone first.
rituals.play: Pick a harmless choice—drink, seat, playlist, shirt, route, snack, order of tasks. Decide privately and act before asking for validation.
rituals.catch: Catch the urge to send the “is this okay?” message after the decision is already safe and reversible.
rituals.reveal: The urge for approval can survive long after permission is actually needed.
rituals.mindBend: A preference does not become valid only after somebody else signs it.

rituals.name: WITNESS LINEUP
rituals.title: WITNESS LINEUP
rituals.targetPattern: Assuming shared memory is identical
rituals.target_pattern: Assuming shared memory is identical
rituals.precise_subpattern: Assuming shared memory is identical
rituals.vibeLine: Memory is not CCTV, even when yours feels 4K.
rituals.hook: Two people can attend the same moment and store different movies.
rituals.predict: Guess which details you know both people would agree on versus details you only remember from your own angle.
rituals.play: List three facts any camera would capture. List three remembered meanings—tone, intention, emphasis, “what they knew.” Mark which items another witness could honestly remember differently.
rituals.catch: Notice where memory ends and interpretation begins.
rituals.reveal: Shared events do not guarantee shared recordings because memory is reconstructed, not replayed.
rituals.mindBend: Two sincere memories can disagree without either person owning a perfect recording.

rituals.name: MOOD-TINTED SCREEN
rituals.title: MOOD-TINTED SCREEN
rituals.targetPattern: Reading a message through current mood
rituals.target_pattern: Reading a message through current mood
rituals.precise_subpattern: Reading a message through current mood
rituals.vibeLine: Interesting—the sender did not edit anything. Your mood did.
rituals.hook: Your phone screen may be clear.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the same message would sound different if you read it after good news.
rituals.play: Take the message bothering you. Imagine receiving it immediately after something that made you feel secure or amused. Read it again in that imagined state.
rituals.catch: Notice which words stay the same while the inferred tone shifts.
rituals.reveal: Our state helps supply the emotional colour of ambiguous communication.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes the screen is neutral and the tint is coming from this side of the glass.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Hinting mistaken for asking
rituals.vibeLine: You may have sent a clue and expected a signed contract.
rituals.hook: Did you make a request—or assign them a mind-reading exam?
rituals.predict: Guess whether the other person could repeat your exact need from the words you actually used.
rituals.play: Recall what you said. Remove tone, facial expression and shared history. Using only the literal words, write what a stranger would think you asked for.
rituals.catch: Compare that with what you hoped the person would understand.
rituals.reveal: Hints feel obvious from inside the mind that created them.
rituals.mindBend: Unspoken needs can feel ignored even when they were never made observable.

Recall what you said. Remove tone, facial expression and shared history. Using only the literal words, write what a stranger would think you asked for.
Guess whether the other person could repeat your exact need from the words you actually used.
Compare that with what you hoped the person would understand. Hints feel obvious from inside the mind that created them.
↻ ASK OR TELEPATHY?

rituals.name: CIRCLE THE BEHAVIOUR

rituals.vibeLine: Specific complaint: useful. Full character assassination: less so.
rituals.hook: We’re putting a circle around what happened—not around the whole human.
rituals.predict: Guess whether anger changes when the complaint is forced to name only an observable behaviour.
rituals.play: Complete: “When they ___, the impact on me was ___.” Ban “selfish,” “toxic,” “lazy,” “bad,” and every other identity label.
rituals.catch: Check if the problem becomes smaller, clearer, or more actionable.
rituals.reveal: Specific behaviour creates boundaries; global labels create fog.
rituals.mindBend: You can reject what someone did without pretending you have finished defining who they are.

rituals.name: CAMERA ZOOM-OUT
rituals.title: CAMERA ZOOM-OUT
rituals.targetPattern: Assuming others notice a small mistake
rituals.target_pattern: Assuming others notice a small mistake
rituals.precise_subpattern: Assuming others notice a small mistake
rituals.vibeLine: Your blooper may not have made anyone else’s highlight reel.
rituals.hook: Your brain has a close-up.
rituals.predict: Guess what percentage of another person’s attention is actually on your mistake right now.
rituals.play: Imagine the scene from a ceiling camera. Include phones, traffic, tasks, conversations, hunger, deadlines—everything competing for everyone’s attention.
rituals.catch: See whether your mistake still occupies the same percentage of the frame.
rituals.reveal: The spotlight effect grows when we confuse our close-up with everyone else’s camera angle.
rituals.mindBend: You are the main character of your attention, not automatically theirs.

rituals.name: THE EMPTY TIMESTAMP
rituals.title: THE EMPTY TIMESTAMP
rituals.targetPattern: A slow response treated as relational evidence
rituals.target_pattern: A slow response treated as relational evidence
rituals.precise_subpattern: A slow response treated as relational evidence
rituals.vibeLine: The clock gave you data. Your brain added gossip.
rituals.hook: There is a delay.
rituals.predict: Guess how many different causes could produce the same response time.
rituals.play: Set the actual delay in one box: “3 hours,” “1 day,” whatever it is. In a second box, list five causes ranging from mundane to negative to positive. Don’t choose among them.
rituals.catch: Notice that the timestamp stayed fixed while the meaning multiplied.
rituals.reveal: Response time is observable. Relationship meaning is inferred.
rituals.mindBend: Silence can contain uncertainty without containing rejection.

Stop comparing your raw damn footage with somebody else’s trailer.

HOOK
If you compare lives, at least compare matching slices.

PREDICT
Guess whether the comparison feels fair if you compare your ordinary Tuesday with their ordinary Tuesday instead of your backstage with their highlight.

PLAY
Take the person you compare yourself with. Replace their visible best moment with an imagined mundane day containing errands, delays, uncertainty and boring admin—just as yours does.

CATCH
Check if the gap changes when the units finally match.

REVEAL
Comparison becomes distorted when one side is a highlight and the other is raw footage.

MIND BEND
A fair comparison needs matching slices, not matching envy.

MOVE ON
↻ SAME-DAY COMPARISON

rituals.title: APOLOGY BORDER CONTROL
rituals.targetPattern: Apologising for having needs or feelings
rituals.target_pattern: Apologising for having needs or feelings
rituals.precise_subpattern: Apologising for having needs or feelings
rituals.vibeLine: Your apology was trying to import everybody’s emotions.
rituals.hook: Not every uncomfortable thing needs an apology visa.
rituals.predict: Guess which part actually belongs to you: behaviour, impact, feeling, need, or someone else’s disappointment.
rituals.play: Take the apology forming in your head. Underline only what you did that violated your own standard. Cross out apologising for existing, feeling, asking, or declining.
rituals.catch: See whether a smaller, cleaner apology remains.
rituals.reveal: Over-apologising can blur accountability by making everything your fault.
rituals.mindBend: Own your behaviour. You do not have to apologise for having a nervous system and boundaries.

rituals.name: COMPLIMENT EVIDENCE LOCK
rituals.title: COMPLIMENT EVIDENCE LOCK
rituals.targetPattern: Positive feedback rejected by changing standards
rituals.target_pattern: Positive feedback rejected by changing standards
rituals.precise_subpattern: Positive feedback rejected by changing standards
rituals.vibeLine: Your inner prosecutor has lost the shredder for thirty seconds.
rituals.hook: Your brain keeps moving the goalposts after praise arrives.
rituals.predict: Guess what explanation your mind will use to dismiss the compliment before you read it again.
rituals.play: Take one genuine compliment. For 30 sec, ban these escape hatches: “they were being nice,” “anyone could do it,” “it was luck,” “it doesn’t count.” Let the statement remain unedited.
rituals.catch: Notice the discomfort of evidence that does not fit the old self-story.
rituals.reveal: Discounting praise protects an existing belief by disqualifying inconvenient data.
rituals.mindBend: If negative evidence counts automatically, positive evidence does not need to pass a secret extra exam.

rituals.vibeLine: Turns out “meant well” and “hurt” can both fit in the same sentence.

rituals.catch: Check if the situation becomes more precise when both lanes stay open.
rituals.reveal: Intent and impact answer different questions.
rituals.mindBend: Harm can be real without proving malice; good intent can be real without erasing harm.

jolly.catch: Compare certainty with access.

PAUSE

jolly.targetPattern: Confidence about another person’s thoughts exceeding access
jolly.mechanismFingerprint: Audit claimed knowledge of another person’s mental state against direct access channels versus inferred content.

rituals.name: WRONG CHANNEL TEST
rituals.title: WRONG CHANNEL TEST
rituals.targetPattern: Sensitive content forced into a poor communication medium
rituals.target_pattern: Sensitive content forced into a poor communication medium
rituals.precise_subpattern: Sensitive content forced into a poor communication medium
rituals.vibeLine: Maybe stop asking six text bubbles to perform a face-to-face job.
rituals.hook: Maybe the conversation is hard because the channel is doing half the damage.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the same message would land differently as text, voice or face-to-face.
rituals.play: Take the issue and imagine it in three channels: short text, phone/voice, in-person. Which parts need tone, speed, pauses or visual cues to be understood?
rituals.catch: Check if the problem includes a medium mismatch, not only a people problem.
rituals.reveal: Communication channels carry different amounts of emotional information.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes you do not need better words. You need a better pipe for the same words.

rituals.target_pattern: One generous act converted into a silent debt
rituals.precise_subpattern: One generous act converted into a silent debt
rituals.vibeLine: That favour may have had invisible payment terms.
rituals.hook: Did you give something—or quietly issue an invoice?
rituals.predict: Guess what you expected back after your helpful act.
rituals.play: Name what you did for them. Finish two versions: “I chose to give this” and “I expected this to earn ___.” Notice which is more accurate.
rituals.catch: Catch any hidden repayment term you never discussed.
rituals.reveal: Generosity and exchange are both valid; resentment grows when one is disguised as the other.
rituals.mindBend: A gift with an invisible repayment clause can feel like betrayal waiting to happen.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Both people trying to be understood at the same time
rituals.vibeLine: Turns out two closing arguments are not a conversation.
rituals.hook: Two microphones are on.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the conflict changes if only one person’s job is understanding for sixty seconds.

rituals.catch: Notice how different “understand first” feels from “reply while listening.”
rituals.reveal: Simultaneous self-defence competes with accurate listening.
rituals.mindBend: Being heard and being agreed with are different jobs.

rituals.name: WHOSE THOUGHT IS THAT?
rituals.title: WHOSE THOUGHT IS THAT?
rituals.targetPattern: One's own fear attributed to another person's likely judgment
rituals.target_pattern: One's own fear attributed to another person's likely judgment
rituals.precise_subpattern: One's own fear attributed to another person's likely judgment
rituals.vibeLine: Interesting how their “opinion” sounds exactly like your insecurity.
rituals.hook: That judgment may have your handwriting on it.
rituals.predict: Guess whether the sentence sounds like something they actually said—or something you fear they might think.
rituals.play: Take the feared judgment. Label it one of three ways: SAID, IMPLIED, or MY FEAR. Don’t upgrade categories without evidence.
rituals.catch: Notice how many social “facts” move into the third box.
rituals.reveal: We can project our own fears into other minds and then react as if they came from outside.
rituals.mindBend: A thought can wear someone else’s face and still be yours.

rituals.name: REQUEST OR SIGNAL?
rituals.title: REQUEST OR SIGNAL?
rituals.targetPattern: Surface request hiding a different relational need
rituals.target_pattern: Surface request hiding a different relational need
rituals.precise_subpattern: Surface request hiding a different relational need
rituals.vibeLine: You may be fighting about the bus instead of where anyone wants to go.
rituals.hook: The request may be asking for more than the literal thing.
rituals.predict: Guess what need sits underneath the request: help, reassurance, respect, closeness, control, certainty, space.
rituals.play: Take one repeated request from you or them. Imagine the literal request is impossible. Ask what emotional outcome the person may still be trying to get.
rituals.catch: Check if the conflict changes when the hidden goal becomes visible.
rituals.reveal: People often argue over the vehicle when the destination is the real issue.
rituals.mindBend: A request can fail while the need beneath it remains understandable.

rituals.name: HOW MANY ORIGINAL OPINIONS?
rituals.title: HOW MANY ORIGINAL OPINIONS?
rituals.targetPattern: Group behaviour mistaken for independent evidence
rituals.target_pattern: Group behaviour mistaken for independent evidence
rituals.precise_subpattern: Group behaviour mistaken for independent evidence
rituals.vibeLine: Consensus looks different when everyone copied the first person.
rituals.hook: Ten people agreeing may contain fewer than ten independent judgments.
rituals.predict: Guess how many of the opinions could have been influenced by earlier opinions.
rituals.play: Take the crowd signal bothering you. Imagine person 2 saw person 1, person 3 saw the first two, and so on. Ask how many truly independent data points might remain.
rituals.catch: Notice how consensus strength changes when influence between people is allowed.
rituals.reveal: Agreement is weaker evidence when opinions are socially linked.
rituals.mindBend: A crowd can echo one signal many times.

rituals.name: DON’T BORROW THEIR VOLUME
rituals.title: DON’T BORROW THEIR VOLUME
rituals.targetPattern: Matching another person's intensity instead of one's own goal
rituals.target_pattern: Matching another person's intensity instead of one's own goal
rituals.precise_subpattern: Matching another person's intensity instead of one's own goal
rituals.vibeLine: Their volume is not a mandatory dress code.
rituals.hook: Their intensity offered you a loan.
rituals.predict: Guess whether your next sentence would be calmer if their tone were neutral.
rituals.play: Imagine the exact same words from them delivered at half the volume. Decide your response from that version, then return to the real conversation.
rituals.catch: Notice how much of your planned response was borrowed from their intensity.
rituals.reveal: Arousal is contagious; goals do not have to be.
rituals.mindBend: You can answer the issue without renting their emotional volume.

rituals.name: WHOSE WORK WAS INVISIBLE?
rituals.title: WHOSE WORK WAS INVISIBLE?
rituals.targetPattern: Remembering one's own effort more vividly than others' effort
rituals.target_pattern: Remembering one's own effort more vividly than others' effort
rituals.precise_subpattern: Remembering one's own effort more vividly than others' effort
rituals.vibeLine: Your own effort came with behind-the-scenes footage. Theirs did not.
rituals.hook: You remember every step of your effort because you lived inside it.
rituals.predict: Guess one thing the other person may have done that you did not witness.
rituals.play: Take a shared task or relationship. List your visible effort. Add three categories of effort they might have contributed outside your view: planning, worrying, travelling, arranging, remembering, recovering.
rituals.catch: Check if the fairness story softens or simply becomes less certain.
rituals.reveal: We have full access to our own effort and partial access to everyone else’s.
rituals.mindBend: Invisible work is easiest to forget when it was not ours.

rituals.vibeLine: One coffee spill did not destroy civilisation.
rituals.hook: Perfect may not be as lovable as your anxiety claims.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you trust a clearly competent person less, more, or the same after one harmless small mistake.

rituals.catch: Notice which version feels easier to connect with.
rituals.reveal: Minor imperfection can increase relatability when basic competence is already established.
rituals.mindBend: A small flaw can lower distance without lowering worth.

rituals.targetPattern: Assuming shared context that was never mutually established
rituals.target_pattern: Assuming shared context that was never mutually established
rituals.precise_subpattern: Assuming shared context that was never mutually established
rituals.vibeLine: You knowing it is not the same as both of you knowing it together.
rituals.hook: You knew it.
rituals.predict: Guess which fact in the disagreement was never explicitly made shared.
rituals.play: Take one assumption and run three checks: Did I know it? Did they know it? Did we both know that the other knew it?
rituals.catch: Notice how fast shared reality becomes thinner than personal knowledge.
rituals.reveal: Communication depends on common ground, not just private information.
rituals.mindBend: A fact can be obvious to you and absent from the shared room.

rituals.name: REQUEST MIRROR
rituals.title: REQUEST MIRROR
rituals.targetPattern: Assuming others are less willing to help than they often are
rituals.target_pattern: Assuming others are less willing to help than they often are
rituals.precise_subpattern: Assuming others are less willing to help than they often are
rituals.vibeLine: You may be charging them more annoyance than you would charge yourself.
rituals.hook: The request feels huge because you are carrying all the embarrassment.
rituals.predict: Guess how burdensome the same small request would feel if someone asked it of you.
rituals.play: Take your request and swap roles. Imagine a decent person asking you the identical favour. Rate how annoyed you would be.
rituals.catch: Compare that rating with what you predict from them.
rituals.reveal: People often underestimate others' willingness to help and overestimate the social cost of asking.
rituals.mindBend: The request can feel heavier in the hand holding it than in the hand receiving it.

rituals.vibeLine: No emoji is not a restraining order.

rituals.catch: Check if absence of warmth had been treated as presence of rejection.
rituals.reveal: No positive signal and a negative signal are not the same data.
rituals.mindBend: Neutral deserves its own box.

VIBE: UNFILTERED

Lack of sunshine is not the same damn thing as a storm.

HOOK
Your social filing cabinet may have only POSITIVE and BAD.

PREDICT
Guess whether this behaviour truly contains negative information or merely lacks positive information.

PLAY
Take the cue—short reply, neutral face, no emoji, quiet greeting. Sort it into POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, or NEUTRAL/UNKNOWN. Don’t force neutral into negative.

CATCH
Check if absence of warmth had been treated as presence of rejection.

REVEAL
No positive signal and a negative signal are not the same data.

MIND BEND
Neutral deserves its own box.

MOVE ON
↻ NEUTRAL GETS ITS OWN BOX

rituals.name: REMOVE THE BADGE
rituals.title: REMOVE THE BADGE
rituals.targetPattern: Role labels changing how a person's behaviour is interpreted
rituals.target_pattern: Role labels changing how a person's behaviour is interpreted
rituals.precise_subpattern: Role labels changing how a person's behaviour is interpreted
rituals.vibeLine: Job title left the room; behaviour stayed.
rituals.hook: The badge may be talking before the person does.
rituals.predict: Guess how you would interpret the same behaviour if you did not know their status, profession, age, or role.
rituals.play: Take one person and mentally remove the label: boss, doctor, junior, parent, expert, influencer. Re-read the behaviour without the badge.
rituals.catch: Notice which assumptions disappear.
rituals.reveal: Status and role labels prime expectations before evidence arrives.
rituals.mindBend: A badge can organise attention without explaining the person.

Your behaviour sometimes teaches your brain how you feel.
jolly.ritualCard:
Your behaviour sometimes teaches your brain how you feel.
Recall a time you helped someone you felt neutral or mildly mixed about. Compare how you saw them before versus after the help.
Guess how your attitude toward someone changes after you voluntarily do them a small harmless favour.
Check if your mind built a warmer explanation for your own behaviour. We sometimes infer attitudes from observing our own actions.
↻ WHY DID I HELP THEM?

rituals.title: ONE LEVEL DEEPER
rituals.targetPattern: Appropriate openness inviting reciprocal openness
rituals.target_pattern: Appropriate openness inviting reciprocal openness
rituals.precise_subpattern: Appropriate openness inviting reciprocal openness
rituals.vibeLine: One level deeper, not emotional scuba diving.
rituals.hook: Connection often moves in small matched steps, not emotional cannonballs.
rituals.predict: Guess what one level deeper than small talk would sound like without becoming oversharing.
rituals.play: Take a safe topic. Move one step from fact to preference, or preference to small personal meaning. Imagine giving the other person room to match or not match it.
rituals.catch: Notice how connection can be invited without demanded intimacy.
rituals.reveal: Moderate self-disclosure often encourages reciprocal disclosure.
rituals.mindBend: Closeness can be offered as a doorway, not thrown like a net.

rituals.title: FIND THE SHARED TEMPO
rituals.targetPattern: Subtle rhythm matching increasing felt connection
rituals.target_pattern: Subtle rhythm matching increasing felt connection
rituals.precise_subpattern: Subtle rhythm matching increasing felt connection
rituals.vibeLine: Same people, less conversational gear grinding.
rituals.hook: Conversations have rhythm before they have meaning.
rituals.predict: Guess whether this person tends to speak fast, slow, pause-heavy, or energetic.
rituals.play: For one harmless conversation, gently match only the pace—not accent, gestures, or personality. Leave it natural.
rituals.catch: Check if turn-taking feels smoother.
rituals.reveal: Subtle temporal synchrony can support affiliation and coordination.
rituals.mindBend: Connection sometimes begins as two nervous systems finding a workable tempo.

rituals.precise_subpattern: Misunderstanding treated as failure instead of normal interactive maintenance
rituals.vibeLine: Misunderstanding found; relationship not declared dead.
rituals.hook: Good conversations are full of tiny repairs nobody remembers.
rituals.predict: Guess what happens if you treat 'Wait, what do you mean?' as maintenance instead of embarrassment.

rituals.reveal: Human communication is noisy and depends on ongoing repair.
rituals.mindBend: Needing clarification is evidence that language is imperfect, not that the relationship is.

rituals.vibeLine: Same words, wildly different imaginary voiceovers.

rituals.reveal: Lean channels force the receiver to reconstruct missing social cues.
rituals.mindBend: Text delivers words efficiently and context badly.

rituals.mindBend: No objection is not identical to endorsement.

rituals.name: MUTUAL KNOWLEDGE CHECK
rituals.title: MUTUAL KNOWLEDGE CHECK
rituals.targetPattern: Publicly shared information influencing coordination more than privately known facts
rituals.target_pattern: Publicly shared information influencing coordination more than privately known facts
rituals.precise_subpattern: Publicly shared information influencing coordination more than privately known facts
rituals.vibeLine: Both knew it. Neither knew the other knew it.
rituals.hook: Knowing the same fact is not always enough; sometimes coordination needs both people to know it is shared.
rituals.predict: Guess what changes when an assumption becomes explicitly mutual.
rituals.play: Take a coordination issue. Say the shared fact out loud or in writing: 'So we're both working from X, right?'
rituals.catch: Notice how mutual certainty differs from parallel private knowledge.
rituals.reveal: Common knowledge supports coordination beyond first-order knowledge.
rituals.mindBend: A shared fact becomes more useful when its sharedness is also shared.

rituals.vibeLine: Your eyebrows may be networking.

rituals.predict: Guess whether your face changes slightly when someone smiles, frowns, or looks tense.

rituals.reveal: People often mimic emotional expressions, which can support shared affect.
rituals.mindBend: Emotion can travel through tiny copied movements before words arrive.

rituals.name: REMOVE THE DEFENCE PARAGRAPH
rituals.title: REMOVE THE DEFENCE PARAGRAPH
rituals.targetPattern: Over-explaining intent crowding out acknowledgment of impact
rituals.target_pattern: Over-explaining intent crowding out acknowledgment of impact
rituals.precise_subpattern: Over-explaining intent crowding out acknowledgment of impact
rituals.vibeLine: Defence lawyer can wait outside.
rituals.hook: Your apology may be trying to prove innocence instead of repair impact.
rituals.predict: Guess which sentence in the apology is mostly there to defend you.
rituals.play: Draft three lines only: what happened, impact you understand, what you will do differently. Move explanation to a separate optional conversation.
rituals.catch: Check if the apology feels clearer without the defence brief.

VIBE: CHEEKY

Good news apparently likes company.

HOOK
A good event can become better when someone helps you notice it again.

PREDICT
Guess whether retelling one small win to an engaged person changes how good it feels.

PLAY
Choose a modest positive event. Tell a trusted person who tends to respond warmly, or write the story as if telling them.

CATCH
Check if the event gains detail or emotional weight.

REVEAL
Positive-event sharing can amplify positive affect and relational closeness.

MIND BEND
Good experiences can compound socially, not only privately.

MOVE ON
↻ JOY GROWS IN THE TELLING

rituals.name: WHO ACTUALLY WANTS THIS?
rituals.title: WHO ACTUALLY WANTS THIS?
rituals.targetPattern: Groups collectively choosing an option nobody privately wants because everyone assumes others want it
rituals.target_pattern: Groups collectively choosing an option nobody privately wants because everyone assumes others want it
rituals.precise_subpattern: Groups collectively choosing an option nobody privately wants because everyone assumes others want it
rituals.vibeLine: Everyone agreed because everyone thought everyone else wanted it.
rituals.hook: A whole group can agree to a plan nobody likes.
rituals.predict: Guess what each person would choose if they were guaranteed nobody would be offended.
rituals.play: For one low-stakes group decision, ask everyone privately or simultaneously: first choice, second choice, and 'I genuinely don't mind.'
rituals.catch: Check if public consensus matches private preference.
rituals.reveal: Groups can coordinate around misperceived preferences.
rituals.mindBend: Agreement is not proof that anyone wanted the result.

rituals.name: LEDGER OR CARE?
rituals.title: LEDGER OR CARE?
rituals.targetPattern: Healthy close relationships sometimes tracking need rather than exact repayment
rituals.target_pattern: Healthy close relationships sometimes tracking need rather than exact repayment
rituals.precise_subpattern: Healthy close relationships sometimes tracking need rather than exact repayment
rituals.vibeLine: Not every coffee requires a forensic invoice.
rituals.hook: Some relationships run on responsiveness, not perfect accounting.
rituals.predict: Guess whether you would want a close person to repay this exact favour or simply care when you need them.
rituals.play: Take one small exchange. Compare LEDGER MODE—equal repayment now—with COMMUNAL MODE—respond to need over time.
rituals.catch: Notice which model actually fits the relationship.
rituals.reveal: Communal relationships often organise giving around need rather than immediate equivalence.
rituals.mindBend: Fair does not always mean identical and immediate.

A crowd is evidence only if the crowd has independent information.
unfiltered.ritualCard:
A crowd is evidence only if the crowd has independent information.
Take the social signal—queue, review, recommendation, reaction. Ask how many independent sources created it.
Guess whether each person chose independently or followed the person before them.
Check if ten people are ten data points or one copied data point. People use others' behaviour as information under uncertainty.

rituals.precise_subpattern: A consistent dissenting view increasing deeper processing even before it changes opinions
rituals.vibeLine: No coup required; one awkward question will do.

rituals.mindBend: Disagreement can improve a decision without winning the vote.

rituals.reveal: People experience their own construal as direct reality.
rituals.mindBend: Shared facts do not guarantee shared meaning.

rituals.ritual_name: YOUR MESS LOOKS WORSE FROM INSIDE IT
rituals.displayName: YOUR MESS LOOKS WORSE FROM INSIDE IT
rituals.targetPattern: One's own vulnerability feeling embarrassing while the same vulnerability in others feels courageous or human
rituals.target_pattern: One's own vulnerability feeling embarrassing while the same vulnerability in others feels courageous or human
rituals.precise_subpattern: One's own vulnerability feeling embarrassing while the same vulnerability in others feels courageous or human
rituals.vibeLine: Apparently vulnerability looks less disastrous when someone else owns it.
rituals.hook: Your vulnerability feels sloppy from the inside and brave from the outside.
rituals.predict: Guess how you would judge a friend for sharing the exact same imperfect admission.
rituals.play: Rewrite your vulnerable sentence as if a respected friend said it to you. Rate warmth, courage, and awkwardness.
rituals.catch: Notice the double standard.
rituals.reveal: People often evaluate their own vulnerable displays more negatively than others do.
rituals.mindBend: The same imperfection can look like failure from inside and humanity from across the table.
rituals.moveOn: ↻ YOUR MESS LOOKS WORSE FROM INSIDE IT

rituals.vibeLine: Less interview, more 'did you see that?'
rituals.hook: Connection can happen sideways—through a shared object, joke, view, problem, or moment.
rituals.predict: Guess whether talking face-to-face about yourselves feels different from jointly noticing the same external thing.

rituals.catch: Notice the 'we saw that' feeling.
rituals.reveal: Shared reality develops when people experience an inner state as common toward the same external target.
rituals.mindBend: Sometimes closeness grows not from staring at each other, but from looking in the same direction.
rituals.moveOn: ↻ LOOK AT THE SAME THING TOGETHER

rituals.name: THREE SIGNALS OF 'I GET YOU'
rituals.title: THREE SIGNALS OF 'I GET YOU'
rituals.targetPattern: Feeling understood, validated and cared for driving closeness more than advice quality alone
rituals.target_pattern: Feeling understood, validated and cared for driving closeness more than advice quality alone
rituals.precise_subpattern: Feeling understood, validated and cared for driving closeness more than advice quality alone
rituals.vibeLine: Fix-it mode has been asked to wait one paragraph.
rituals.hook: People often remember whether they felt understood before they remember your brilliant advice.
rituals.predict: Guess which signal is missing: understood, validated, cared for.
rituals.play: In one supportive reply, include one line for each needed signal: 'I hear X,' 'that makes sense because Y,' 'I'm with you / what would help?'
rituals.catch: Notice how the response feels different from jumping to solutions.
rituals.reveal: Perceived responsiveness is central to intimacy and relationship wellbeing.
rituals.mindBend: Connection often begins with 'you make sense to me,' not 'here is the fix.'
